description:
A rebuild whose watched inputs moved in timestamp but not in content leaves every test target fresh, so watching four repository roots costs nothing on a branch switch.

## Background

The build script is triggered by timestamps on the directories it watches. A branch switch rewrites untouched files, so the script re-runs on content that did not change. If that run rewrites its destinations regardless, the whole test topology relinks — the same class of regression an earlier change removed from this build script by making it read nothing ambient, measured then at roughly three minutes.

The workspace's build-footprint budget does not cover this. It counts integration-test targets and sums test-executable bytes; neither reads the build output directory and neither observes invalidation. So the property that makes the watch affordable is, today, an expectation rather than a measurement, and it was never measured in this workspace at all.

The seeded-repository harness can observe it: cold-build the isolated repository, touch a watched input without changing its content, rebuild, and ask how many test artifacts were not fresh.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A rebuild after a timestamp-only change beneath a watched root leaves the test targets fresh, relinking none of them.
- [hard] REQ-02: The assertion runs in an isolated seeded repository, so it never depends on the state of the working checkout.
- [hard] REQ-03: A failure names the targets that relinked, so the reader sees the cost rather than a bare mismatch.
- [hard] REQ-04: The assertion distinguishes a relink caused by the watched roots from one caused by an unrelated input, so it reports the property it is named for.
title: Pin the assembly's freshness on a timestamp-only change
